# Sirach Chapter 30 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 30 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**Council Notes:**
Chapter 30 opens with extensive, unabashedly pro-corporal-punishment instruction on child-rearing (vv. 1-13). The council notes that this reflects ancient Israelite pedagogical assumptions (cf. Prov 13:24, 23:13-14) not universally endorsed by modern readers, but it is translated faithfully. The chapter transitions sharply to a meditation on health vs. wealth (vv. 14-17), with the famous "death is better than a bitter life" statement (v. 17). The bizarre vv. 18-20 liken good things given to a sick person to offerings given to an idol or to a eunuch's encounter with a virgin — all cases of frustrated capacity. The chapter closes with a warm endorsement of joy, cheerfulness, and mental health (vv. 21-25), forming a positive counterweight to the harsh opening.

V. 20's eunuch image is deliberately stark. It is the image of total incapacity — cruelest precisely because the desire remains while the capacity is gone.

---

**30:1** He who loves his son will keep on chastising him, so that he may rejoice over him in the end and not grieve before his neighbors.

**30:2** He who disciplines his son will profit from him and will boast of him among his acquaintances.

**30:3** He who educates his son will make his enemy envious, and before his friends he will rejoice over him.

**30:4** The father dies, and it is as if he has not died; for he has left behind one like himself.

**30:5** In his lifetime he saw him and rejoiced over him, and at death he was not grieved.

**30:6** Against his enemies he left behind an avenger, and toward his friends one who returns kindness.

**30:7** He who coddles his son will bind up his wounds, and at every outcry his heart will be shaken.

**30:8** An unbroken horse turns stubborn, and a son left to himself turns headstrong.

**30:9** Pamper your child and he will terrify you; play with him constantly and he will make you grieve.

**30:10** Do not laugh everything off with him, lest you end up weeping with him; in the end you will gnash your teeth.

**30:11** Do not give him freedom in his youth, and do not ignore his follies.

**30:12** Bow down his neck in his youth and beat his sides while he is still young, lest he become stubborn and refuse to obey you, bringing grief to your soul.

**30:13** Discipline your son and labor over him, lest his shameful behavior cause you to stumble.

**30:14** Better is a poor man who is healthy and strong in body than a rich man who is afflicted in his flesh.

**30:15** Health and soundness of body are better than all gold, and a vigorous body than boundless wealth.

**30:16** There is no wealth better than health of body, and there is no pleasure better than joy of heart.

**30:17** Death is better than a bitter life, and eternal rest better than chronic illness.

**30:18** Good things poured before a mouth that is closed are like offerings placed before a tomb.

**30:19** What benefit is an offering to an idol? It cannot eat or smell. So too the one who is afflicted by the LORD —

**30:20** seeing with his eyes and groaning, as a eunuch who embraces a virgin and sighs.

**30:21** Do not give yourself over to sorrow, and do not torment yourself in your own deliberation.

**30:22** Gladness of heart is a man's life, and the joy of a man is length of days.

**30:23** Console yourself and cheer your heart; and drive sorrow far from you, for sorrow has destroyed many, and there is no gain in it.

**30:24** Envy and anger shorten life, and worry brings on old age before its time.

**30:25** A cheerful and good heart will take care in its food, and his meals will be a pleasure.
